content.question_text: Why did the designers bother with interfaces when there are abstract classes?

core_requirements: To support multiple inheritance of type (a class can implement multiple interfaces) while avoiding the diamond problem.
Because Java does not allow multiple inheritance of classes (you can only extend one class).
acceptable_variations: Because Java doesn't allow multiple inheritance, you can extend only one class.
To allow a class to inherit contracts from multiple sources.

content.question_text: Which interface is common across all classes that manage sequences of characters?
Can you add static methods to an interface?
Can a method be private in an interface?
Before interfaces could hold static methods, what was the common practice for where to put utility methods connected to a certain interface?

core_requirements: To put them in a companion class whose sole job was to hold utility methods (e.g., Collection/Collections, Path/Paths).
acceptable_variations: In a separate utility class paired with the interface.

content.question_text: Why are companion classes no longer needed for interface utility methods?

core_requirements: Because interfaces can now hold static methods directly.
acceptable_variations: Since static methods can now be placed in interfaces.

content.question_text: When a method is private in an interface, what is its use limited to?

core_requirements: It is limited to being a helper method for other methods (default or static) of the same interface.
acceptable_variations: Cannot be used outside the interface.

content.question_text: What is a default method when it comes to interfaces?

core_requirements: A method that has a default implementation provided directly inside the interface.
acceptable_variations: A method with a default implementation.
A method you don't have to implement unless you want to override it.

content.question_text: What does it mean for a class when a method is default in an interface?

core_requirements: It means you do not need to implement the method, but you can override it if needed.
acceptable_variations: You don't have to implement it.

content.question_text: What does it mean that default methods allow interfaces to evolve?

core_requirements: Older classes that implement the interface won't break if a new method is added to the interface with a default implementation.
It maintains both source and binary compatibility.
acceptable_variations: You can add new methods without breaking existing code.
